claims.title: Alexander the Great conquers Bactria
claims.summary: Alexander of Macedon overruns Bactria and the lands of modern Afghanistan in a gruelling campaign, leaving Greek garrisons and settlers that seeded later Hellenistic kingdoms.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Afghanistan: Crossroads of empires, from Bactria and the Bamiyan Buddhas to the Durrani state and the wars of the modern age.", terralore.co/country/AFG/chronicle#ev-329bce-alexander-the-great-conquers-bactria, claim TL:AFG:event:329bce:alexander-the-great-conquers-bactria, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Greco-Bactrian kingdom
claims.summary: Diodotus I breaks Bactria away from the Seleucid empire to found the independent Greco-Bactrian kingdom, a Hellenistic state that fused Greek and local traditions north of the Hindu Kush.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Afghanistan: Crossroads of empires, from Bactria and the Bamiyan Buddhas to the Durrani state and the wars of the modern age.", terralore.co/country/AFG/chronicle#ev-256bce-the-greco-bactrian-kingdom, claim TL:AFG:event:256bce:the-greco-bactrian-kingdom, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Kushan empire and Gandhara art
claims.summary: Under rulers such as Kanishka the Kushans build an empire across Bactria and Gandhara, spreading Buddhism along the Silk Road and giving rise to the Greco-Buddhist Gandhara school of sculpture.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Afghanistan: Crossroads of empires, from Bactria and the Bamiyan Buddhas to the Durrani state and the wars of the modern age.", terralore.co/country/AFG/chronicle#ev-127-the-kushan-empire-and-gandhara-art, claim TL:AFG:event:127:the-kushan-empire-and-gandhara-art, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Bamiyan Buddhas carved
claims.summary: Monks carve two colossal Buddhas, about 55 and 38 metres high, into the cliffs of the Bamiyan Valley, a great centre of Buddhist pilgrimage on the routes through the Hindu Kush.

sources.label: Cultural Landscape and Archaeological Remains of the Bamiyan Valley

claims.title: Arab conquest and the coming of Islam
claims.summary: Arab Muslim forces take Herat in the wake of the conquest of Persia, beginning the gradual and long-contested Islamisation of the Afghan lands.

sources.label: Afghanistan: A Country Study
sources.publisher: Library of Congress, Federal Research Division

claims.title: Mahmud of Ghazni and the Ghaznavid empire
claims.summary: Sultan Mahmud of Ghazni builds a vast empire from Afghanistan into Iran and India and turns his capital Ghazni into a centre of Islamic culture and learning.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Afghanistan: Crossroads of empires, from Bactria and the Bamiyan Buddhas to the Durrani state and the wars of the modern age.", terralore.co/country/AFG/chronicle#ev-998-mahmud-of-ghazni-and-the-ghaznavid-empire, claim TL:AFG:event:998:mahmud-of-ghazni-and-the-ghaznavid-empire, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Ghurids sack Ghazni
claims.summary: The Ghurids of central Afghanistan overthrow Ghaznavid power, sacking Ghazni and extending Muslim rule into northern India; their Minaret of Jam survives as a UNESCO World Heritage site.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Afghanistan: Crossroads of empires, from Bactria and the Bamiyan Buddhas to the Durrani state and the wars of the modern age.", terralore.co/country/AFG/chronicle#ev-1150-the-ghurids-sack-ghazni, claim TL:AFG:event:1150:the-ghurids-sack-ghazni, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Herat, capital of the Timurid renaissance
claims.summary: Shah Rukh moves the Timurid capital to Herat, where he and Queen Gawhar Shad make the city a dazzling centre of architecture, poetry and miniature painting.

sources.label: Afghanistan: A Country Study

claims.title: Ahmad Shah Durrani founds the Afghan state
claims.summary: A jirga at Kandahar elects Ahmad Shah Durrani ruler after Nadir Shah's death; the Durrani Empire he founds is regarded as the origin of the modern Afghan state.

sources.label: Ahmad Shah Durrani — History, Empire & Accomplishments

claims.title: First Anglo-Afghan War
claims.summary: Britain invades to install a friendly ruler but is overwhelmed; a British-Indian force is destroyed during its disastrous 1842 retreat from Kabul, an early clash of the Great Game.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Afghanistan: Crossroads of empires, from Bactria and the Bamiyan Buddhas to the Durrani state and the wars of the modern age.", terralore.co/country/AFG/chronicle#ev-1839-first-anglo-afghan-war, claim TL:AFG:event:1839:first-anglo-afghan-war, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Second Anglo-Afghan War and the Treaty of Gandamak
claims.summary: Britain invades again over fears of Russian influence; the 1879 Treaty of Gandamak gives Britain control of Afghan foreign affairs in return for subsidy and protection.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Afghanistan: Crossroads of empires, from Bactria and the Bamiyan Buddhas to the Durrani state and the wars of the modern age.", terralore.co/country/AFG/chronicle#ev-1878-second-anglo-afghan-war-and-the-treaty-of, claim TL:AFG:event:1878:second-anglo-afghan-war-and-the-treaty-of, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Durand Line drawn
claims.summary: Amir Abdur Rahman Khan agrees the Durand Line with British India, fixing a frontier that divides Pashtun communities and remains a source of dispute with Pakistan to this day.

sources.label: Afghanistan: A Country Study
sources.publisher: Library of Congress, Federal Research Division

claims.title: Independence and the Treaty of Rawalpindi
claims.summary: Amir Amanullah Khan repudiates British control of foreign affairs and, after the Third Anglo-Afghan War, secures the Treaty of Rawalpindi (8 August 1919) recognising Afghan control of its own foreign relations.

sources.label: Third Afghan War and the Revolt in Waziristan

claims.title: Amanullah's reforms collapse
claims.summary: Sweeping modernising reforms provoke tribal and religious revolt; Amanullah Khan abdicates and flees into exile in January 1929, plunging the country briefly into civil strife.

claims.title: The long reign of Zahir Shah
claims.summary: Mohammad Zahir Shah rules for four decades of cautious modernisation and neutrality, introducing in 1964 a constitution that opens a brief era of parliamentary politics.

claims.title: Daoud Khan founds the republic
claims.summary: Mohammad Daoud Khan overthrows his cousin Zahir Shah in a bloodless coup, abolishes the monarchy and proclaims Afghanistan a republic with himself as president.

claims.summary: The communist PDPA overthrows and kills President Daoud Khan, seizing power in the Saur Revolution and imposing radical reforms that ignite armed rebellion across the country.

claims.title: The Soviet invasion
claims.summary: Soviet forces invade on 24 December 1979, kill the Afghan leader Hafizullah Amin and install Babrak Karmal, beginning a decade-long war against the US-backed mujahideen.

claims.title: Soviet withdrawal
claims.summary: Under the 1988 Geneva Accords the Soviet Union pulls out; the last troops leave on 15 February 1989 after a war that killed huge numbers of Afghans and displaced millions.

claims.title: Collapse of the communist government and civil war
claims.summary: Najibullah's government falls in 1992 and rival mujahideen factions turn on one another, devastating Kabul in a civil war that opens the way for the Taliban.

claims.title: The Taliban capture Kabul
claims.summary: The Taliban, led by Mullah Omar, seize Kabul and proclaim the Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan, imposing a severe religious order and isolating the country internationally.

claims.title: Destruction of the Bamiyan Buddhas
claims.summary: The Taliban dynamite the colossal sixth-century Buddhas of Bamiyan as idolatrous, destroying a unique monument of world heritage months before their own fall.

claims.title: US-led intervention topples the Taliban
claims.summary: After the 11 September attacks a US-led coalition and the Northern Alliance overthrow the Taliban; the Bonn Agreement of December 2001 installs Hamid Karzai's interim government.

claims.title: Taliban return to power
claims.summary: Following the 2020 Doha agreement and the withdrawal of foreign forces, the Afghan government collapses and the Taliban retake Kabul on 15 August 2021, re-establishing the Islamic Emirate.
